chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mu'awiya ibn Hukaym, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Khath'ami, from Ishaq ibn Ammar.

He said: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'At what [distance] is the shortening [of prayer]?' He said: 'At a barid. Woe to them! As if they had not performed hajj with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and [they] shortened [prayers].'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: taqsir/qasr — shortening of the four-unit (raka'at) prayers during qualifying travel
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: barid — a unit of distance equal to four farsakhs (~22 km), given here as the minimum threshold
key_terms.وَيْحَهُمْ: wayḥahum — 'woe to them'; an expression of the Imam's frustration at those who contest this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance for shortening prayers (qasr) according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Ishaq ibn Ammar asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the minimum travel distance that makes shortening (taqsir/qasr) of prayers obligatory, and the Imam rules it to be one barid (approximately four farsakhs, ~22 km). The Imam's exclamation 'woe to them!' (wayḥahum) sharply rebukes those who dispute this established ruling, appealing to the undeniable precedent of the Prophet's (SAWW) own practice of shortening prayers during the hajj pilgrimage.
